Theory vs what you drew
What to notice
As n grows the histogram of means turns into a bell whatever the population looks like — even one that is lopsided or only ever 0 or 10. That is the Central Limit Theorem: for large n (9758 uses n ≥ 30 as the rule of thumb), X̄ ~ N(μ, σ²/n) approximately.
The centre stays at μ, but the spread shrinks like σ²/n: four times the sample size, a quarter of the variance. Compare the s² of your means with σ²/n.
With n = 1 a “mean” is just one value, so the histogram is the population itself — the blue curve does not fit it at all.
